detailed_findings.finding: Closure under addition is complete and correctly split into the three residue cases, with proper use of the assumptions for i+j<m and i+j>m.
The co-finiteness proof is logically sound: defining M=max{x_1,...,x_{m-1}} and showing every n>=mM lies in S_x suffices.
The multiplicity proof correctly shows m is in S_x, no positive integer below m is in S_x, and every non-multiple element of S_x exceeds m.

reason: The proof establishes all required parts of the lemma: S_x is a submonoid of Z_{>=0}, its complement is finite, and its least positive element is m. The closure argument correctly handles all residue cases and uses exactly the stated Kunz-type inequalities in the needed subcases i+j<m and i+j>m. The co-finiteness argument is valid via the bound n>=mM implying the quotient q in n=qm+r satisfies q>=M, hence q>=x_r for each residue r>0. The multiplicity argument correctly excludes all positive integers < m and shows any non-multiple in S_x is > m. There is no substantive semantic drift from the lemma sketch or its role in the assembly.
